channel.title: Bios on Chen lab
channel.description: Recent content in Bios on Chen lab

item.title: About Jana Hadas
item.description: Research Background I joined Dr. Chen’s lab early 2022 as lab manager. Our lab is focusing on pediatric kidney cancer, which brought me back to microscopy to see beautiful images of developmental stages of kidney tumors in mice. Previously, I worked in the Departments of Pharmacology (with insect cells and parasites) and Neurology (on COVID-19), and every job has expanded my knowledge and enriched me. When I’m not in the lab Science is also involved in my hobbies.

item.title: About Chelcea Zamora
item.description: Research Background My current role in the lab is maintaining the animal colony, providing research support, I was granted the opportunity to join the Chen lab in October of 2021. I was excited to learn about all the different studies and new developments with pediatric patients. I love meeting new people and working with animals. When I’m not in the lab When I am not in the Lab, you can find me spending most of my time with my daughter Raelynn and my husband Justin.

item.title: Bendu Konneh
item.description: Research Background My first professional exposure to research was in a urological oncology lab studying molecular biomarkers of testicular germ cell tumors. After a year, I was granted the opportunity to join the Chen Lab and contribute to research related to genetic drivers of pediatric cancers. Currently, my role in lab is to provide administrative laboratory support and maintain the rodent breeding colonies. When I’m not in the lab/hospital I spend much of my time devouring content related to true crime and macabre human history in the form of podcasts and documentaries.

item.title: Taylor Hartshorne
item.description: Research Background My research experience began at New Mexico State University while taking an independent research lab course for my Bachelor’s degree. Once I saw how the information that I had learned in my genetics classes could be applied in the lab to solve real-life problems, I was hooked. I am excited to further my research experience by studying pediatric cancer in the Chen lab prior to applying to medical school, for the specialty is a great way to merge my academic interest in molecular genetics and personal passion for working with children.

item.title: Kenneth Chen
item.description: Research Background As a child, I wanted to study dinosaurs when I grew up. Their might and their majesty left me in awe: these monsters once ruled the earth, yet ultimately they could not survive the progress of time and became relics of biological history. Today, I study a different kind of monster: childhood cancer. While we’ve made great progress, more children still die of cancer than any other disease in the US.

item.title: Claudette Fraire
item.description: Research Background I first got interested in research while doing a DNA extraction experiment from cheek cells. For my bachelor’s degree, I attended Texas Woman’s University where I participated in various research projects seeking to understand unusual DNA structures, impacts on DNA from UV radiation, and the mechanism of carboplatin. During my time as an undergraduate, I participated in a summer internship at UT Southwestern where I studied Wilms tumor. Since that incredible experience I have made it my career goal to study pediatric cancer.

item.title: Lane Beeman
item.description: Research Background My research experience is filled with a variety of animal models, enjoying the challenges and skillset required for each one. My current role in the lab is maintaining the animal colony, providing research support, and executing all experiments using the animal model. I joined the Chen lab in November of 2019 because I was excited to learn more about Wilms tumor and DICER1 Syndrome and to make a difference in lives of pediatric patients.

item.title: About Patricia Tiburcio
item.description: Research Background I first caught the research bug in 2010 when I joined the Protein Structure and Immunology Laboratory at the University of the Philippines Diliman. I joined the effort in defining the altering landscape of integrins during cancer progression as my undergraduate thesis. After I spent a year working with the Dengue Research Group at St Luke’s Medical Center in Quezon City, Philippines, I moved to Salt Lake City, Utah.

item.title: About Lindsay Mendyka
item.description: Research Background I started working in biomedical research in Spring 2014 at UT Southwestern Medical Center. I became very fluent in animal breeding, handling, and dosing techniques. I translated this experience to pediatric cancer research and produce animal models to better understand DICER1 Syndrome. I thoroughly enjoy learning new techniques and procedures and applying them to our research, which is my favorite thing to do while in the lab. I enjoy challenges and teaching my newly acquired knowledge and skills to other lab members.

item.title: About Peter Schoettler
item.description: Research Background I’ve been involved with researching Pleuropulmonary Blastoma (PPB), a rare Pediatric lung cancer, and DICER1 Syndrome, a cancer predisposition syndrome, since 2006. My sister and brother were the 3rd and 10th cases of PPB, and a DICER1 mutation runs through my family, which has inspired my career trajectory and research focus. In 2006, the genetic cause of PPB was still unknown, but now we know that mutations in the microRNA processing enzyme, DICER1, causes a wide variety of tumors within DICER1 Syndrome.
